title: The Signal in the Middle Window

The player, as Watson, chooses the posture in which the night operation begins. Concise but load-bearing: the light means Helen has done her part and the window may stand ready.

player_desire: To act at once and not fail the woman waiting across the dark road.
live_pressure: The signal is up; every delay may cost Helen her life, yet a misstep could ruin the plan or spring a trap.

title: Staging the Trap
treatment: Staging the vigil inside the middle bedroom. Shoes slipped off, shutters noiselessly closed, lamp moved and then turned down. Holmes whispers the operational rules: no sound, no light, stay awake, pistol ready. The player arranges the room — revolver on the table corner, cane, matches, candle — for either safer defence or stronger observation.
runtime_goal: Let the player configure the vigil space and internalize the fatal rules of silence and darkness, expressing proof-vs-protection through how the room is staged.
player_desire: To be ready for whatever comes without making the one sound that could be fatal.
live_pressure: Holmes warns the least sound would be fatal and any light would be seen through the ventilator; the trap must be set in near-total silence.
opening_image: Inside the middle bedroom all is as you saw it by day, yet each object has drawn into a more sinister relation; Holmes's whisper is so low you must read it from his lips, the cane laid on the bed, the matches and candle at his hand.

title: The Dreadful Vigil
treatment: The dreadful vigil. Absolute darkness, no sound, not even a breath. The player inhabits felt time: the parish clock booming every quarter, twelve through three, the occasional night-bird, and once at the very window the long catlike whine of the cheetah at liberty. Nothing happens, and that is the point.
runtime_goal: Stretch felt time so silence and uncertainty are truly experienced before the violent reversal, making the climax land.
player_desire: To endure the wait, stay awake and alert, and not break the silence.
live_pressure: Endless darkness and strain; the cheetah is loose outside, and the attack could come at any unknown moment.
opening_image: The shutters cut off the least ray of light, and in the absolute darkness you cannot hear even the drawing of a breath, though you know Holmes sits open-eyed a few feet away; far off the parish clock booms the quarter.

title: The Gleam at the Ventilator

A momentary gleam of light shows in the direction of the ventilator, then vanishes, succeeded by a strong smell of burning oil and heated metal — someone next door has lit a dark-lantern. A gentle sound of movement, then silence, and the smell grows stronger through the strained half-hour.

title: The Strike and the Cry
treatment: The reversal. A very gentle soothing sound, like a small jet of steam from a kettle. Holmes springs from the bed, strikes a match, and lashes furiously at the bell-pull, yelling 'You see it, Watson?' The sudden glare blinds Watson; a low clear whistle sounds; Holmes's face is deadly pale with horror and loathing. Then the most horrible cry breaks from the night and swells and dies.

title: The Speckled Band

Roylott sits in his grey dressing-gown, bare ankles, red Turkish slippers, the dog-whip across his lap, chin cocked upward, eyes fixed in a rigid stare. Round his brow a peculiar yellow band with brownish speckles — which begins to move, rearing the squat diamond head of a snake. 'The band! the speckled band!'

title: The Swamp Adder Contained
treatment: Containment and moral verdict. Holmes cries 'It is a swamp adder — the deadliest snake in India,' notes Roylott died within ten seconds, and speaks the maxim that violence recoils upon the violent and the schemer falls into his own pit. He draws the dog-whip from the dead man's lap, nooses the reptile's neck, carries it at arm's length, and thrusts it into the iron safe, closing it.

title: The Debrief and the Verdict
treatment: The debrief and final synthesis. Holmes lays out the rational retrospective chain as interactive Q&A: his erroneous first conclusion from insufficient data (the gipsies, the word 'band'), his reconsideration when danger could come from neither window nor door, the ventilator and dummy bell-rope, the clamped bed as a bridge for something passing through, the snake, the untraceable Eastern poison, the whistle to recall it, the milk to train it. Then the evidence (chair-standing, safe, saucer of milk, whipcord, the metallic clang of the safe door) and his admission that he lit the light and attacked, driving the snake back to turn upon its master. Compressed per guidance into one closing room, ending on the authored justice-vs-discretion choice.
runtime_goal: Assemble the complete rational solution and moral coda through player-driven questioning, confirm the recoil causality, and close the session on how the truth should live afterward.
player_desire: To understand exactly how the murder worked and how Holmes turned it back on Roylott.
live_pressure: The night is won, but the full truth is still unspoken; Watson (and the player) must piece together how it was done and decide how it should be carried into the world.
opening_image: The lamp-light falls hard upon the iron safe, the saucer of milk, the chair beneath the ventilator, and the dummy bell-rope in its true character; Holmes, grave and composed after his hardest labours, sets the chain before you point by point.

"The discovery that this was a dummy, and that the bed was clamped to the floor, instantly gave rise to the suspicion that the rope was there as a bridge for something passing through the hole and coming to the bed."

"I heard the creature hiss as I have no doubt that you did also, and I instantly lit the light and attacked it." ... "And also with the result of causing it to turn upon its master at the other side."
exit_condition: The pressure resolves when the full clue-to-inference chain and the recoil causality are understood, and the player has chosen the moral authorship of the case record — the final cash-out of the session.
next_bridge: For one moment, at least, the matter rests in the cold light of reason, and that is a relief not lightly valued. Yet the same objects which have yielded up the method now seem to ask another question: by what account shall such facts pass from this room into the world beyond it?
